name: Ego4D
summary: Ego4D is a massive-scale egocentric video dataset assembled by a consortium spanning nine countries: roughly 3,670 hours of unscripted daily activity recorded from head-mounted cameras by hundreds of unique participants, with dense timestamped narration and a suite of benchmark tasks. For robotics its value is not the benchmarks but the raw distribution it captures: human hands manipulating real objects in real homes and workplaces, at a scale no teleoperation fleet will ever reach.
innovation: Scale and diversity of first-person manipulation footage, gathered by a coordinated multi-institution capture effort with a consent and de-identification protocol.
Dense natural-language narration aligned to timestamps, giving the video language grounding for free.
matters: The pretraining corpus behind R3M, GR-1 and most of the human-video branch.
Reframed the data bottleneck as something potentially solvable without robot hardware.
limits: No action labels, no robot embodiment, no force or tactile signal — closing that gap is the entire research problem.
Passive observation only: no failures deliberately explored, no counterfactuals, no interventions.
lineage: The root of the human-data branch: the first corpus large enough to make action-free human video a credible pretraining source.
